Night Cream for Oily Skin: How to Choose and Use One

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 4 October 2026Updated 16 October 20265 min read
Quick answer

Yes, oily skin still needs a night cream. Washing removes moisture as well as oil, and skin that is left dry can look shinier the next day. Choose a light, non-greasy texture, use a thin layer on clean skin, and add less on the oiliest areas.

  • Texture: light and quick to absorb
  • Amount: smaller than a pea, thinner on the T-zone
  • Avoid harsh, stripping cleansers
  • Patch test if you break out easily

If your face is shiny by lunchtime, putting more cream on it at night sounds like a terrible idea. Plenty of people with oily skin skip moisturiser for exactly that reason. It usually backfires.

Oil and moisture are not the same thing. Oily skin can still be short of water, and skin that has been dried out often looks shinier, not less. The right night cream for oily skin, used the right way, leaves it calmer and more balanced. Here are six rules that make it work.

Does oily skin really need a night cream?

Yes. Washing your face takes off oil, sweat and sunscreen. It takes off moisture too. If nothing goes back on, your skin feels tight, and by the next afternoon it looks shinier than ever. A light layer of cream at night keeps it comfortable and smoother-looking by morning.

6 rules for a night cream for oily skin

1. Use less than you think you need

This is the one that matters. Half a pea for the whole face. Most of what people blame on a cream comes down to using too much of it.

2. Put it where you need it

Oily skin is hardly ever oily all over. Cheeks and jaw tend to need more than the forehead and nose. Start with the drier parts and use whatever is left on your fingers for the rest.

3. Wash properly first

If you wore sunscreen or make-up, cleanse twice in the evening: an oil-based cleanser, then a gentle face wash. Cream on top of leftover sunscreen and dust is what blocks pores.

4. Look for ingredients that help

  • Niacinamide (vitamin B3). A favourite for a smoother, less shiny look.
  • Aloe vera. Light and fresh.
  • Hyaluronic acid. Hydration with no heaviness.
  • Kojic acid. For the look of marks left by pimples.

5. Give it ten minutes

Let the cream settle before your face meets the pillow. It absorbs better, and your pillowcase stays clean.

6. Change with the weather

In humid months, use the thinnest layer you can manage. In winter, or if you sleep with the AC on, oily skin often wants a bit more.

Best night cream for oily skin: how to pick one

There is no single best night face cream for oily skin. The best one is the cream you can use in a thin layer every night without your face feeling heavy. Check these four things before you buy:

  1. Texture. Light creams and gel-creams are easiest. A richer cream works too, in a very thin layer.
  2. Ingredients. Niacinamide, aloe vera and hyaluronic acid are good signs. Heavy butters and lots of fragrance are less helpful on oily skin.
  3. Jar size. Oily skin needs very little cream, so a small jar to start with lets you try a cream without wasting money.
  4. How your skin feels after a week. Comfortable, not tight, not greasy. That is the only test that counts.

Can oily skin use a rich cream?

It can, as long as you follow the first two rules. A rich cream in a very thin layer often does better than a watery gel slapped on thickly. Warm it between your fingertips, press it onto the cheeks first, and only then spread what is left over the forehead and nose.

Oily skin in the monsoon and humid months

Humid weather makes oily skin feel greasier, and many people stop using cream completely. Keep going, but use a very thin layer, skip the forehead and nose if they already feel slick, and let the cream settle under a fan for ten minutes before bed. More in the monsoon skin care routine.

What to stay away from

  • Skipping moisturiser completely.
  • Washing your face more than twice a day.
  • Harsh scrubs and toners loaded with alcohol.
  • Going to bed in sunscreen or make-up.

A night routine that takes two minutes

  1. Oil cleanser, then a gel face wash.
  2. A light, alcohol-free toner.
  3. Half a pea of night cream, mostly on the cheeks.

For the morning half, open the skincare routine builder and choose the oily option. The application method is in how to apply night cream.

If you break out

A few small spots in the first week can happen with any new product. If they keep coming, use less, switch to every second night, or stop. Acne that will not go away is a medical matter and worth a visit to a dermatologist. There is more in avocado night cream side effects.

Read next: Avocado cream for oily skin, Hyaluronic acid night cream.

Short answers

Every day? Yes, thinly.

Gel or cream? Either. The amount matters more than the type.

Will it make me oilier? Not if you use a small amount on clean skin.

Can I use a day cream at night? Yes, if it has no sunscreen in it. Sunscreen is not needed at night.

How much should I use? Half a pea for the whole face, a little more on dry cheeks.

What about oily skin with acne? Keep the cream light and the amount small, and see a dermatologist for acne that keeps coming back.
